question: You are caring for a stroke patient who has trouble swallowing (dysphagia). What must you check first before giving them anything to eat or drink?

options.A: Perform a proper swallow screen and ensure the patient sits upright
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Give the patient a large glass of cold water to test throat reflexes
options.D: Place the patient completely flat on their back in bed

explanation: Swallowing issues put patients at high risk of choking or getting food in their lungs (aspiration). Always check their swallow reflex and keep them sitting upright!

question: Why shouldn't we rely solely on 'we've always done it this way' when caring for patients?

options.A: Old routines are rarely supported by current evidence
options.B: Textbooks change their definitions every single month
options.C: Hospital management strictly forbids the use of tradition
options.D: Patients refuse care that has been used for many years

explanation: It is easy to stick to old habits, but checking modern research helps us give our patients the safest, most up-to-date care possible.

question: What happens in the kidneys during cystinuria to cause stone formation?

options.A: Rapid enzymatic breakdown of calcium in the glomerulus
options.B: Impaired renal tubular reabsorption of specific amino acids
options.C: Reduced hepatic production of filtering enzymes
options.D: Excessive dietary intake of sulfur-containing proteins

explanation: Think of the kidneys like a recycling plant! In cystinuria, a little genetic mix-up stops the kidneys from reabsorbing certain amino acids back into the body. This causes cystine to build up in the urine and form stones. You've got this!

question: How do open drug markets make self-medication so easy?

options.A: They provide easy, unrestricted access to potent drugs without a prescription
options.B: They operate under strict government supervision to prevent drug abuse
options.C: They offer free laboratory tests to help patients choose the right drug
options.D: They employ clinical pharmacologists who safely evaluate every customer

explanation: Open markets let anyone walk in with cash and walk out with strong, serious medications—no questions asked by a medical professional.

question: When is skeletal traction usually taken off?

options.A: When the patient is ready for surgery, casting, or healing allows
options.B: As soon as the patient gets bored on bed rest
options.C: When the pin site develops normal crusting
options.D: Exactly 24 hours after the pin was put in

explanation: You got it! Skeletal traction is a temporary helper. It comes off once definitive care like surgery or a cast takes over, or when the bone is stable enough.

question: Why are maternity homes so important in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They replace federal tertiary teaching hospitals completely
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medications during labor
options.C: They offer free surgical care funded by international donors
options.D: They serve as local bridges to care when distant hospitals are hard to reach

explanation: Spot on! By being close by, they bridge the gap so mums don't have to travel huge distances just to get basic care.

question: Why should a patient stay sitting upright for about 30 minutes after eating?

options.A: To allow the nurse enough time to clear the bedside table
options.B: To prevent food reflux and reduce the risk of aspiration
options.C: To encourage the patient to fall into a deep sleep
options.D: To help the digestive enzymes break down fats faster

explanation: Staying upright gives the stomach a head start on digesting, stopping food or acid from creeping back up into the throat.

question: What is the main focus of medical treatment for someone sick with yellow fever?

options.A: Providing supportive care to manage symptoms and organ failure
options.B: Giving heavy doses of antibiotics to prevent secondary bacterial infections
options.C: Performing emergency surgery to remove the infected liver tissue
options.D: Administering a specific antiviral drug to destroy the virus quickly

explanation: Correct! Since there's no magic cure pill for the virus yet, treatment is all about supporting the patient's body until they fight it off. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a health promotion program?

options.A: To increase the cost of purchasing imported drugs
options.B: To check if the program achieved its goals and used resources effectively
options.C: To prove that the government needs no further assistance
options.D: To find reasons to dismiss junior healthcare staff

explanation: Evaluation helps determine what worked well, what failed, and how future health interventions can be improved. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h9)

question: Why are items like sugary soft drinks left out of standard food groups?

options.A: They are too expensive for rural families to buy
options.B: They contain too much water and zero calories
options.C: They spoil too quickly in warm tropical climates
options.D: They offer little to no real nutritional value

explanation: Exactly! Dietary scores focus on nutrient-packed foods that actually build health, rather than empty calories.

question: Why is the retina at the back of the eye so important?

options.A: It produces the lubricating fluid inside the eyeball
options.B: It changes color to match the surrounding environment
options.C: It contains cells that turn light into nerve signals
options.D: It acts as a hard shield against physical injury

explanation: The retina holds special cells that catch light and change it into electrical signals for your brain to understand. Great job reviewing this!

question: What is the proper way to cut fingernails during routine care?

options.A: In a rounded shape with deep side corners
options.B: As short as possible down to the quick
options.C: In a deep V-shape to expose the nail bed
options.D: Straight across following the natural curve

explanation: Great thinking! Cutting straight across and avoiding digging into the corners helps protect your patient from painful ingrown nails.

question: What is the golden rule when conducting a home visit for a family planning defaulter?

options.A: Announce the client's medical history loudly to all neighbors
options.B: Maintain strict confidentiality and protect client privacy
options.C: Bring local community leaders to witness the counseling session
options.D: Leave written flyers on the front door for everyone to read

explanation: Privacy is vital! Protecting the client's medical information keeps them safe from community gossip or partner backlash.

question: In research, what does the term 'reliability' mean?

options.A: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure
options.B: The speed at which the patient answers interview questions
options.C: Consistency of results when using a tool repeatedly
options.D: How expensive the laboratory equipment is to purchase

explanation: Spot on! If a tool is reliable, it gives you stable, dependable results every time you use it under the same conditions.

question: What is the main purpose of achieving high community vaccination coverage?

options.A: Ensuring pharmaceutical companies sell enough medication each year
options.B: Preventing chronic non-communicable illnesses like diabetes
options.C: Creating herd immunity to protect vulnerable people who cannot be vaccinated
options.D: Eliminating the need for any handwashing or sanitation practices

explanation: When most of the community is vaccinated, germs have a hard time spreading, which keeps fragile individuals safe. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do nursing performance standards need to be clear and specific instead of vague?

options.A: Vague statements are illegal for hospitals to publish
options.B: Staff nurses refuse to read guidelines that contain descriptive words
options.C: Objective standards can be accurately measured and evaluated
options.D: Hospital accountants will not approve funding for subjective rules

explanation: When standards are clear and specific, every supervisor evaluates them the same way, making feedback fair and helpful.

question: What is the best way for a community nurse to stop the spread of diarrhoea in a village?

options.A: Providing mosquito nets for sleeping areas at night
options.B: Teaching proper handwashing with soap and safe water storage
options.C: Inspecting local houses for structural roof damage
options.D: Distributing high-dose antibiotic capsules to all households

explanation: Diarrhoea germs usually spread through the faecal-oral route via dirty hands and water. Simple hygiene education and clean water storage save lives!

question: Facing discrimination over a long period of time causes which physical response in the body?

options.A: Enhanced muscle growth and physical strength
options.B: Persistent stress and elevated cortisol levels
options.C: Permanent immunity to common infections
options.D: Immediate decrease in blood pressure

explanation: Discrimination acts as a constant stressor, keeping stress hormones like cortisol high and wearing down a person's health over time. Keep learning!

question: You notice raw, red skin inside a patient's nostrils while getting ready to put on a nasal cannula. What should you do first?

options.A: Scrub the irritated skin vigorously with an antiseptic alcohol wipe
options.B: Switch the patient immediately to an invasive mechanical ventilator
options.C: Refuse to start the oxygen therapy until the skin is completely healed
options.D: Document the finding, apply a water-based lubricant if ordered, and monitor the area closely

explanation: Always check and document skin status! Protecting sore areas with safe, water-based lubricants helps prevent further friction without stopping vital oxygen.

question: What two measurements are used to calculate cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) in the brain?

options.A: Mean arterial pressure and intracranial pressure
options.B: Systolic blood pressure and respiratory rate
options.C: Heart rate and central venous pressure
options.D: Oxygen saturation and core body temperature

explanation: You find the CPP by taking the mean arterial pressure and subtracting the intracranial pressure. You've got this formula down!

question: In pharmacology, what is a drug receptor?

options.A: A specific protein structure on or inside a cell
options.B: A specialized blood vessel in the liver
options.C: A type of chemical filter in the kidneys
options.D: An enzyme that breaks down waste products

explanation: Picture a receptor as a tiny lock on a cell surface, and the drug is the key that fits into it to start an action.

question: Which type of bacterial toxin is released only when the bacterial cell wall breaks apart?

options.A: Exotoxins
options.B: Coagulase
options.C: Endotoxins
options.D: Antitoxins

explanation: Endotoxins stay tucked inside the outer wall of certain bacteria (Gram-negative) and are only set free when the bacteria break down.

question: Who is primarily protected by the proper use of UN-certified transport packaging?

options.A: Hospital administrators managing the facility budget
options.B: Healthcare workers, couriers, and the general public
options.C: Patient family members waiting in the clinic lobby
options.D: Only the laboratory technicians performing the final analysis

explanation: Dangerous goods transit involves many handlers outside the hospital walls, making spill prevention vital for community health and safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: What is a great lifestyle step to help restore regular ovulation in a patient with PCOS and insulin resistance?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of dietary protein
options.B: Strict bed rest for several weeks
options.C: Complete elimination of dietary water
options.D: Weight management and regular exercise

explanation: Lifestyle is powerful medicine! Getting regular exercise and managing weight helps the body handle insulin better, which naturally helps balance hormones and restore ovulation.

question: A patient with severe liver failure has generalized edema and slow-healing wounds. What is the best nursing action to evaluate their nutrition?

options.A: Advise the patient to eliminate all proteins from their hospital diet
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of plain water daily
options.C: Measure the patient's blood pressure every fifteen minutes
options.D: Review daily weights, fluid balance charts, and serum albumin levels

explanation: You're a natural! Tracking daily weights, fluid charts, and albumin levels gives you the clear picture you need on fluid shifts and protein status.

question: What do macroeconomic indicators provide for a country?

options.A: A numerical snapshot of economic health
options.B: A count of registered nurses
options.C: Individual patient health records
options.D: Hospital room occupancy rates

explanation: Macroeconomic indicators give a broad numerical summary of how a nation's economy is performing overall. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is a major cause of waterborne and vector-borne diseases in local communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of modern private clinics
options.B: Inadequate portable water and poor waste disposal
options.C: Over-reliance on indoor physical exercise equipment
options.D: Strict adherence to universal sterile protocols

explanation: You got it! Without safe water and proper trash or sewage disposal, germs spread quickly and cause waterborne and insect-spread illnesses.

question: Which clinical sign tells you a patient is slipping into dangerous septic shock?

options.A: Localized redness and swelling around a surgical incision
options.B: High white blood cell count without any fever present
options.C: Dangerously low blood pressure unresponsive to fluids
options.D: Increased urine output caused by excessive fluid intake

explanation: Spot on! In septic shock, blood vessels relax so much that blood pressure plummets dangerously low and stubbornly refuses to bounce back, even after giving IV fluids.

question: Which level of prevention stops risk factors from even starting through broad social and economic policies?

options.A: Clinical rehabilitation
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Primordial prevention is all about stopping risk factors before they even take root in a society through broad policies.

question: Your patient just came back from abdominal surgery. Their tummy feels a bit swollen and you can't hear any bowel sounds. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Administer a strong laxative orally right away
options.B: Massage the abdomen vigorously to force gas out
options.C: Encourage the patient to eat a large solid meal
options.D: Keep the patient NPO until bowel activity returns

explanation: If the bowel isn't moving (paralytic ileus), giving food or drink will only cause nausea and vomiting. Keeping them NPO (nothing by mouth) keeps them safe until peristalsis wakes up!

question: Why do nurse managers use bar charts instead of long tables of numbers?

options.A: To permanently replace patient electronic health records
options.B: To hide missing data from hospital inspectors
options.C: To make quick comparisons between different groups easier
options.D: To comply with strict legal prescribing laws

explanation: Visual bars let healthcare staff spot differences in workload or patient metrics much faster than reading numbers in a table. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why can psychological abuse be just as damaging as physical abuse?

options.A: It prevents the body from ever healing from minor infections
options.B: It destroys self-worth and creates profound fear and total dependency
options.C: It is easily diagnosed through standard blood and urine tests
options.D: It always leads directly to permanent paralysis within days

explanation: You nailed it! Psychological abuse strips away a person's self-belief and traps them in deep fear, making it incredibly hard for them to walk away. You're developing true clinical empathy.

question: What exactly are 'Pick bodies' seen under a microscope in brain tissue?

options.A: Scars from previous traumatic head injuries
options.B: Deposits of calcium in the brain blood vessels
options.C: Clumps of abnormal tau protein inside nerve cells
options.D: Infections caused by bacteria in the spinal fluid

explanation: Pick bodies are just microscopic clumps of tangled tau protein. When neurons get weighed down by these clumps, they start to struggle and break down.

question: What does the accessibility principle mean in youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Staff members must speak at least three local languages fluently
options.B: Services must be affordable, conveniently located, and open at suitable times
options.C: Healthcare workers must visit every school in the community monthly
options.D: Clinics must provide free medications for all chronic illnesses

explanation: Accessibility ensures that cost, location, and operating hours do not prevent young people from getting the care they need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why is it important to teach patients how to navigate parties, weddings, and restaurants during dietary counselling?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever eating junk food again
options.B: It proves that the nurse knows more than the patient
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will lose weight in one week
options.D: Real life includes parties and restaurants where strict rules do not fit

explanation: Brilliant thinking! Life is full of celebrations and social gatherings. Teaching flexible problem-solving helps patients stay healthy without missing out on the joy of living.

question: Which of these heart rhythms needs an immediate emergency shock?

options.A: Sinus Bradycardia
options.B: Ventricular Fibrillation
options.C: Asystole
options.D: Pulseless Electrical Activity

explanation: Ventricular Fibrillation (VF) is a shockable rhythm because the heart still has wild electrical activity that a shock can clear. Flatlines (asystole) need chest compressions and meds, not shocks!

question: What are the three classic signs of Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Chest pain, high fever, and skin rash
options.B: Tremors, stiffness, and slow movement
options.C: Eye problems, poor balance, and confusion
options.D: Severe headache, stiff neck, and sudden paralysis

explanation: Great job! Watch out for trouble with eye movements, unsteady walking, and confusion—they form the classic triad.

question: Why do nurses look at time, place, and person (descriptive epidemiology) during an outbreak?

options.A: It punishes health workers who failed to report early cases
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory blood and stool testing
options.C: It helps form clues about who is getting sick and where the source might be
options.D: It guarantees that no new patients will contract the disease tomorrow

explanation: Spotting patterns in who is falling sick, where, and when helps us hunt down where the disease came from and how to stop it.

question: If your ward has a severe shortage of nursing assistants, what is a likely result for you as the registered nurse team leader?

options.A: Being exempted from all clinical ward duties
options.B: Having more time to focus purely on complex patient management
options.C: Spending extra time performing basic domestic or clerical chores
options.D: Automatic promotion to hospital director

explanation: That's correct! When support staff are missing, professional nurses often have to step in to cover basic tasks, which cuts into time for leadership and assessments.

question: What makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care (EmONC) center different from a basic one?

options.A: The ability to perform blood transfusions and Caesarean sections
options.B: The presence of pediatricians in the delivery room at all times
options.C: The requirement that mothers stay in the hospital for a full month
options.D: The exclusive use of traditional herbal remedies for pain

explanation: When things get tough, a comprehensive center can handle surgeries like C-sections and give blood transfusions—things basic clinics can't do. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: Which hormone gets a major boost in release during deep, slow-wave sleep?

options.A: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.B: Growth hormone
options.C: Parathyroid hormone
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Deep sleep triggers a big release of growth hormone, which helps your body repair tissues and recover from the day's stress.

question: As your patient breathes, what normal movement should you see in the water seal chamber fluid?

options.A: Rapid foaming accompanied by a sudden drop in fluid level
options.B: Complete stillness with no movement of the water column
options.C: Tidaling, where the water level rises and falls with respirations
options.D: Vigorous, continuous bubbling indicating active air leaks

explanation: Correct! This gentle rising and falling is called tidaling, and it tells you that the chest tube system is working properly with the patient's breathing.

question: What common struggle among family caregivers should you always watch out for during follow-up visits?

options.A: Excessive financial wealth
options.B: Overconfidence in surgical skills
options.C: Desire to change careers
options.D: Burnout and depression

explanation: Looking after someone with a long-term brain condition is heavy work, both physically and emotionally. Always check in on how the caregivers are holding up!

question: Which sign tells you that a limb in traction has poor blood flow?

options.A: The ability to wiggle all toes easily on command
options.B: Cold toes and a slow capillary refill over four seconds
options.C: Warm skin and a strong pulse in the foot
options.D: Normal pink coloration of the nail beds

explanation: Great job thinking through circulation checks! Cold toes and sluggish refill are classic warning signs that pressure or swelling is slowing down blood flow.

question: Which agency leads public health disease control and surveillance right here in Nigeria?

options.A: Standards Organisation of Nigeria
options.B: Federal Ministry of Education
options.C: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control
options.D: National Union of Road Transport Workers

explanation: Well done! The NCDC is our national public health body that takes charge of tracking outbreaks and keeping us prepared.

question: What is a major challenge when trying to run team nursing in many Nigerian hospital wards?

options.A: High patient-to-nurse ratios and severe staff shortages
options.B: Complete lack of patients admitted to the wards
options.C: Too many nursing assistants available for every shift
options.D: An excessive number of registered nurses on every ward

explanation: Spot on! Shortages of professional staff make leading teams tough because nurses get overworked and stretched across too many duties.

question: Which layer of the pleura hugs the outer surface of the lungs tightly?

options.A: Mediastinal pleura
options.B: Parietal pleura
options.C: Diaphragmatic pleura
options.D: Visceral pleura

explanation: You've got this! Think of the visceral pleura as the inner skin that sticks right onto the lung tissue. Great job keeping up with your anatomy!

question: Which of these is NOT a common health system barrier to getting children immunized?

options.A: Unreliable electricity supply for vaccine refrigerators
options.B: Excessive availability of solar-powered refrigerators in rural posts
options.C: Frequent stockouts of syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Poor road networks delaying transport to remote areas

explanation: Having plenty of working solar fridges would actually solve problems, not cause them! Bad roads, power cuts, and shortages are the real barriers we fight daily.

question: What life-threatening emergency happens when fluid overload backs up all the way into the lungs?

options.A: Pleural mesothelioma
options.B: Chronic bronchial asthma
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Acute pulmonary edema

explanation: When the kidneys can't clear fluid, it backs up into the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs, causing acute pulmonary edema and severe breathing distress. You're mastering critical care concepts!

question: What must a participant give before answering a research questionnaire?

options.A: Proof of health insurance
options.B: A physician's referral letter
options.C: A notarized identity card
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after being fully informed about the study's purpose. Ethical nursing practice starts here!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge for monitoring and evaluation in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Inconsistent electricity and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Staff shortages and heavy workloads for nurses
options.C: Fatigue from filling out multiple paper registers
options.D: Unlimited budgets and an excess of electronic tablets

explanation: Resource-limited settings are known for budget constraints and shortages, so having unlimited funds and excess tablets is definitely not the norm!

question: An older patient seems to be losing their hearing, but it's actually a simple, fixable blockage. What is it?

options.A: Cerumen impaction
options.B: Cochlear hair cell death
options.C: Tympanic membrane scarring
options.D: Auditory nerve atrophy

explanation: Cerumen impaction is just a fancy word for heavy earwax buildup! Once you clean it out, the patient's hearing usually pops right back to normal.

question: Why do doctors test breast cancer tissue for HER2 receptors?

options.A: It tells the doctor exactly how many months the patient has to live
options.B: It prevents the cancer from spreading to the bone marrow
options.C: It proves the patient has a family history of endocrine disorders
options.D: It identifies tumors that may respond to specific HER2-blocking medications

explanation: Finding HER2 helps doctors target the cancer directly with specialized medications that block these specific growth signals. Modern medicine is amazing like that! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where in the digestive tract does the absorption of almost all nutrients happen?

options.A: Esophagus
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the superstar of absorption! Its lining is specially designed to soak up digested nutrients straight into the bloodstream.

question: A patient from a fishing community presents with blood in their urine and lower belly pain. Which parasite is the likely cause?

options.A: Necator americanus
options.B: Enterobius vermicularis
options.C: Schistosoma species
options.D: Ascaris lumbricoides

explanation: Schistosoma parasites can damage the bladder and urinary tract lining, causing blood in the urine (hematuria) and discomfort.

question: What is the main purpose of a referral pathway in humanitarian GBV response?

options.A: To ensure that nurses do not have to provide any clinical treatment
options.B: To force every patient to repeat their traumatic story to multiple agencies
options.C: To transfer patient debt records to international banking organizations
options.D: To connect survivors with coordinated medical, legal, and shelter services

explanation: A referral pathway links different support groups together so the patient gets total care without missing steps or getting bounced around blindly.

question: What does the term intersectionality describe in patient care?

options.A: The physical meeting point where blood vessels cross in the body
options.B: The exact moment when a patient transitions from childhood to adulthood
options.C: How multiple social identities overlap to shape unique life experiences
options.D: How biological sex interacts strictly with inherited genetic diseases

explanation: Intersectionality highlights that factors like race, gender, and class combine to influence a person's unique health realities and challenges. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the amazing brain process that helps a person recover and build new nerve pathways after an injury?

options.A: Neurogenesis
options.B: Apoptosis
options.C: Neuroplasticity
options.D: Homeostasis

explanation: Think of neuroplasticity as the brain's superpower! It is the nervous system's ability to change, reorganize, and form fresh connections after damage occurs, helping patients bounce back.

question: A patient on hydrochlorothiazide complains of feeling very weak and dizzy. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink less water throughout the day
options.B: Discontinue the medication immediately without consulting the doctor
options.C: Check the most recent serum electrolyte laboratory results
options.D: Instruct the patient to increase daily dietary table salt intake

explanation: Well reasoned! Weakness and dizziness can mean electrolytes are out of whack. Always check the lab results to see what's happening with potassium and sodium.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you realize a medication error has happened?

options.A: Write an angry message in the chat group for the next shift
options.B: Call the hospital lawyer to prepare legal defense documents
options.C: Hide the empty medication wrapper in a pocket to destroy evidence
options.D: Assess the patient's clinical condition and provide any needed emergency care

explanation: The patient always comes first! Checking on their physical condition and providing any necessary care takes priority over paperwork and reporting.

question: Which body system controls the release of hormones that trigger puberty?

options.A: Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
options.B: Sympathetic-adrenomedullary pathway
options.C: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis
options.D: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system

explanation: Well done! The HPG axis is the body's master control center for releasing the sex hormones that drive all those physical changes during puberty.

question: As a nurse, why is it important to look beyond obvious physical injuries when checking for abuse?

options.A: Because abusers always come along to every hospital visit
options.B: Because physical injuries always heal completely without leaving emotional scars
options.C: Because hospital rules do not allow us to write down emotional abuse
options.D: Because victims often come in with vague aches and pains instead of visible cuts or bruises

explanation: You've got this! Abuse shows up in many hidden ways. Patients might visit the clinic complaining of ongoing headaches, tiredness, or belly pain rather than obvious trauma.

question: What is the main reason conflict happens in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Having too many registered nurses on a single ward
options.B: Working an excessive number of consecutive night shifts
options.C: Strict adherence to hospital operational policies
options.D: A clash of values, goals, or needs between people

explanation: Conflict simply pops up when people interact and their personal values, goals, or needs don't match up. It happens to everyone, even the best healthcare teams!

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an allergic reaction after administering eye drops?

options.A: A slight bitter taste in the back of the mouth
options.B: Mild coolness on the surface of the skin
options.C: Sudden swelling and itching around the eye
options.D: Temporary blurriness right after the drop falls

explanation: Swelling, intense itching, and hives indicate an allergic immune response to the medication ingredients. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: Who needs to be right there at the bedside when a very early preterm baby is delivered?

options.A: The hospital administrator and billing officers
options.B: An orthopedic surgeon and surgical assistants
options.C: A specialized hospital social worker and dietician
options.D: Neonatal resuscitation and paediatric team members

explanation: Teamwork is everything in the labour ward! Having the neonatal experts ready ensures the tiny newborn gets immediate respiratory help. Fantastic clinical judgment!

question: Which medication do doctors commonly start early in pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia in women with sickle cell disease?

options.A: High-dose hydroxyurea
options.B: Low-dose aspirin
options.C: Therapeutic penicillin
options.D: Intravenous iron sucrose

explanation: Brilliant! Low-dose aspirin is a helpful tool started early on to protect the placenta and lower the risk of pre-eclampsia.

question: What is a constant physical challenge when nursing on a moving ship?

options.A: Frequent electrical storms inside underground tunnels
options.B: Exposure to extreme desert heat and blowing sand
options.C: Constant rolling, pitching, and vibrating of the vessel
options.D: Lack of oxygen due to high altitude mountain climbing

explanation: Exactly! The natural movement of the water means the ship is always moving, which makes doing clinical procedures a unique challenge.

question: Why is a community diagnosis compared to an individual physical examination?

options.A: Because nurses must examine every single resident physically
options.B: Because community members are treated inside a hospital ward
options.C: Because diagnosis always requires a laboratory blood test
options.D: Because health problems must be assessed before treatment is planned

explanation: Just as a clinician diagnoses an individual patient before giving medicine, public health workers assess a community to design the right health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: A female client reports a thick vaginal discharge and spotting after intercourse. Which condition should you suspect first as a nurse?

options.A: Ovarian cysts
options.B: Uterine fibroids
options.C: Cervicitis
options.D: Cystitis

explanation: Unusual discharge paired with bleeding after sex are classic clues pointing right to cervical inflammation.

question: Where must the urine drainage bag be placed relative to the patient's bladder at all times?

options.A: Resting directly on the patient's chest
options.B: Below the level of the bladder
options.C: Level with the mattress surface
options.D: Hanging from the top bed rail

explanation: Gravity is your friend here! Keeping the bag lower than the bladder stops urine from flowing backward and causing an infection.

question: Which situation is an example of cross-contamination from poor glove habits?

options.A: Not wearing gloves to take a pulse on an arm
options.B: Touching a computer keyboard with gloves you wore during wound care
options.C: Washing your hands right after taking off both gloves
options.D: Choosing a larger glove size to avoid thumb tears

explanation: Using dirty gloves on shared equipment like keyboards transfers patient germs to surfaces where other staff can pick them up.

question: What is the main way airborne chemical vapors and dust particles quickly enter the bloodstream?

options.A: Inhalation through the lungs
options.B: Direct absorption through intact skin
options.C: Injection via superficial capillaries
options.D: Ingestion through the stomach

explanation: Our lungs have a huge surface area and a rich network of tiny blood vessels, making breathing in dusts or gases the fastest route right into our general circulation.

question: Which eye condition is an absolute contraindication for anticholinergic medications?

options.A: Conjunctivitis
options.B: Cataracts
options.C: Color blindness
options.D: Glaucoma

explanation: Anticholinergics dilate the pupil, which can trap fluid inside the eye and dangerously worsen glaucoma. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is the main reason for using strict aseptic technique during an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To keep the doctor's hands clean during the procedure
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the patient
options.C: To prevent introducing bacteria that cause septic arthritis
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the bloodstream

explanation: Strict sterility protects the joint capsule from dangerous bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why can TypeIV FGM sometimes be hard for healthcare providers to spot right away?

options.A: It always heals without leaving any form of scar tissue.
options.B: It may involve subtle modifications like piercing or scraping rather than major tissue amputation.
options.C: It only affects internal organs that cannot be seen during a physical exam.
options.D: It is performed exclusively using sterile surgical lasers.

explanation: Because Type IV can involve smaller cuts or piercings, it might not look like the traditional, larger tissue removal seen in other types.

question: When planning exercises for a patient whose cancer has spread to the bones, what must you guard against?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Pathological fractures
options.C: Acute kidney injury
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Bones weakened by cancer metastases are very fragile. We must avoid high-impact movements to prevent unexpected bone breaks.

question: A client taking daily ibuprofen for knee osteoarthritis tells the nurse they noticed dark, tarry stools. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Tell the client to drink more water and double their daily walking distance
options.B: Suggest that the client switch to taking the pain pill on an empty stomach
options.C: Instruct the client to stop the ibuprofen and report the finding to the provider immediately
options.D: Explain that dark stools are a normal side effect of all joint medications

explanation: Dark, tarry stools indicate upper gastrointestinal bleeding, a serious complication of NSAID use that requires immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: Your patient just returned to the ward after a modified radical mastectomy. What is a key nursing action to prevent lymphedema?

options.A: Encouraging heavy weightlifting with the affected arm to improve strength
options.B: Keeping the affected arm hanging low by the bedside all day long
options.C: Applying a tight tourniquet to the affected arm every morning for exercise
options.D: Instructing the patient to avoid blood pressure checks and injections on the affected arm

explanation: Protect that arm! No BP cuffs, no needles, and no IV lines on the surgery side to keep the lymph fluid flowing smoothly.

question: What is the main cause of drug resistance in patients taking HIV treatment?

options.A: Inconsistent medication adherence allowing viral replication during low drug levels
options.B: Eating heavy fatty meals right before taking the evening dose
options.C: Swallowing pills with cold water instead of warm water
options.D: Storing medication bottles in brightly lit hospital rooms

explanation: Spot on! Missing doses leaves gaps where drug levels drop, giving the virus room to multiply and mutate against the medication.

question: A community nurse partners with local farmers and school headmasters to combat child malnutrition. Which concept does this action best demonstrate?

options.A: Private health insurance
options.B: Intersectoral linkages
options.C: Tertiary medical isolation
options.D: Acute hospital management

explanation: Partnering with agriculture and education sectors to address malnutrition is a classic example of intersectoral linkages. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: A breastfeeding mother says she feels mild lower tummy cramps whenever her baby nurses. How can you explain this?

options.A: This is an abnormal sign of postpartum hemorrhage requiring immediate review
options.B: Oxytocin released during breastfeeding also causes the uterus to contract
options.C: Estrogen levels are dropping too quickly and causing muscle spasms
options.D: The baby is pressing too hard against the mother's abdomen during feeding

explanation: It's totally normal! The same oxytocin that helps push milk out also gives the uterus gentle little squeezes to help it shrink back to its pre-pregnancy size.

question: Which blood type is known as the universal red cell donor because almost anyone can safely receive it in emergencies?

options.A: Type AB positive
options.B: Type B negative
options.C: Type A positive
options.D: Type O negative

explanation: You've got this! Type O negative red cells have no main antigens, so they won't trigger an attack in most recipients.

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for Pick's disease?

options.A: Restoring lost brain tissue in the frontal lobe
options.B: Reversing the underlying cellular tau accumulation
options.C: Curing the primary neurodegenerative process
options.D: Managing behavioral symptoms and improving comfort

explanation: Since we can't cure or reverse the disease yet, our nursing care focuses on keeping the patient comfortable, calm, and managing tough behavioral symptoms.

question: What is the main purpose of giving a blood transfusion to a patient with acute haemorrhage?

options.A: To prevent the kidneys from producing any urine
options.B: To speed up the digestion of food in the stomach
options.C: To replace lost red blood cells and restore oxygen delivery
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Transfusions supply the red blood cells needed to carry oxygen to tissues when the patient's own blood volume is dangerously depleted. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h6)

question: Why are transcutaneous (skin) bilirubin readings often followed up with a blood test when numbers are high?

options.A: Skin devices can be influenced by skin tone and are only meant for screening
options.B: Transcutaneous meters measure direct bilirubin instead of total bilirubin
options.C: Skin readings only work accurately after the baby is two weeks old
options.D: Blood tests are required by law before a baby can start breastfeeding

explanation: Handheld skin scanners are wonderful for quick checks, but a blood test gives us the exact numbers needed for treatment decisions.

question: When would a nurse researcher build a conceptual framework instead of using a single theoretical framework?

options.A: When combining ideas from multiple sources to fit a unique study
options.B: When the researcher wants to avoid reading published literature
options.C: When the study has no human participants involved
options.D: When the hospital administration bans the use of theories

explanation: Sometimes one theory isn't enough! When your study has a unique mix of ideas, you blend them together into your own custom conceptual framework.

question: A researcher studies whether a new walking program lowers blood pressure in elderly patients. What is the dependent variable?

options.A: Blood pressure level
options.B: The researcher conducting the study
options.C: The walking program
options.D: The age of the elderly patients

explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome being measured, which in this case is the patient's blood pressure responding to the exercise. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care.

question: Which of the following will NOT typically cause prevalence to increase?

options.A: An increase in new infections
options.B: A long duration of the illness
options.C: Migration of sick people into the town
options.D: A high death rate from the disease

explanation: A high mortality rate removes people from the population quickly, which lowers prevalence rather than raising it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What term describes the natural, gradual decline of the immune system as people age?

options.A: Seroconversion
options.B: Hypersensitivity
options.C: Immunization
options.D: Immunosenescence

explanation: You got it! Immunosenescence simply means the immune system gets a bit tired and weaker as we age.

question: How do upright or side-lying positions help a mum whose baby is in a tricky position?

options.A: They prevent the mother from feeling any sensation of pressure.
options.B: They use gravity to encourage the fetus to rotate into a more favorable position.
options.C: They widen the cervix mechanically without the need for medications.
options.D: They completely stop all painful uterine contractions for a few hours.

explanation: Spot on! Gravity is your free assistant in the labour ward. Shifting positions helps the baby wiggle into a better angle.

question: A student is found to have a severe heart murmur during a routine school check. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Ignore the finding since the child looks healthy
options.B: Refer the student to a specialized pediatric clinic
options.C: Instruct the class teacher to prescribe medication
options.D: Send the child home permanently from school

explanation: Serious conditions detected during school screenings require formal referral to medical specialists for proper diagnosis and management. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: When is the best time to document a rectal suppository in the patient's records?

options.A: Immediately after the procedure is completed
options.B: Before gathering the supplies from the cart
options.C: At the end of the entire nursing shift
options.D: Only if the patient complains of pain later

explanation: Charting right away keeps your records accurate and prevents medication errors. Great job keeping up with your duties!

question: A mother wants to mark her newborn baby for protection. How should the nurse best handle this counseling?

options.A: Threaten to call security if she attempts the procedure
options.B: Perform the cuts safely using hospital surgical blades
options.C: Explain infection risks gently and suggest safer alternatives
options.D: Ignore the conversation because it is a private family matter

explanation: That's brilliant nursing! Respectful education bridges cultural beliefs with health safety without pushing the client away.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to stop drug theft in a pharmacy store?

options.A: Conducting surprise physical counts of valuable medicines
options.B: Installing security cameras around the dispensing counters
options.C: Restricting key access to authorized storekeepers only
options.D: Leaving the main storage room unlocked during lunch breaks

explanation: Leaving storage rooms unlocked is an open invitation for missing inventory! Security requires locked doors and controlled access.

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and birth attendants in community maternal health programs?

options.A: They provide financial loans to build local maternity clinics
options.B: They can legally perform emergency surgeries in villages
options.C: They help encourage early reporting of danger signs and prompt referral
options.D: They replace the need for professional midwives entirely

explanation: Spot on! Partnering with community influencers bridges traditional practices with modern healthcare, making sure mothers get to the clinic on time. Excellent perspective!

question: What is a common cause of accidental poisoning among young children in many Nigerian households?

options.A: Commercial industrial solvents kept in clinical labs
options.B: Prescription antihypertensive tablets left on tables
options.C: Imported cosmetics applied to the skin
options.D: Kerosene stored in empty beverage bottles

explanation: Storing hazardous fuel in familiar soft drink containers easily misleads thirsty children, leading to accidental ingestion and severe aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h3)

question: Why is a low salt diet frequently prescribed in clinical practice?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood sugar
options.B: To stimulate a faster metabolic rate
options.C: To reduce strain on the heart and blood vessels
options.D: To increase the body's overall fluid retention

explanation: Excess salt causes water retention which raises blood pressure, so restricting salt lightens the workload on the cardiovascular system. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h1)

question: What is the best way to report a patient's death when calling the doctor?

options.A: Provide a concise report of assessment findings and absent vital signs
options.B: Wait until the morning shift change before making the phone call
options.C: Ask the physician for permission to start post-mortem care immediately
options.D: Ask the doctor to sign the death certificate over the telephone

explanation: Well done! Giving quick, clear facts helps the doctor understand what's happening before they even step into the room.

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake in a paper health register?

options.A: Apply thick correction fluid until the page is blindingly white.
options.B: Scratch it out heavily with a pen until it is totally hidden.
options.C: Draw a single neat line through the mistake, write 'error', and sign beside it.
options.D: Rip out the page and rewrite the whole day's entries.

explanation: Never scribble out or use heavy Tipp-Ex on medical records! A single neat line keeps things legal, honest, and easy to read while showing an official correction was made.

question: A home care nurse is helping a diabetic patient manage blood sugar using local Nigerian foods. What is the best approach?

options.A: Insist the patient only eat imported foods recommended in standard textbooks
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether until blood sugar normalizes
options.C: Ignore the diabetes and let the patient eat whatever they want
options.D: Adapt the diabetic meal plan using accessible local staples and traditional foods

explanation: Brilliant! Good nursing means working with familiar, local foods so the patient can easily stick to their health plan.

question: In simple terms, what is atelectasis?

options.A: An abnormal collection of air in the pleural cavity
options.B: A severe bacterial infection inside the lung tissue
options.C: The collapse or closure of a lung resulting in reduced gas exchange
options.D: High pressure inside the blood vessels of the lungs

explanation: Correct! Atelectasis happens when tiny air sacs (alveoli) deflate or collapse, making it harder to trade gases.

question: Why is being sharp with clinical assessments extra important for a midwife working in a home setting?

options.A: Hospital policies dictate every step of home interventions
options.B: Advanced surgical equipment is always readily available
options.C: Clients at home never experience sudden medical complications
options.D: The midwife must rely on independent skills without immediate backup

explanation: When you are out in the field doing a home birth, there is no doctor or emergency trolley around the corner. Your own assessment skills are the first line of defense!

question: A patient with a back injury to the vertebrae has damage in which body cavity?

options.A: Thoracic cavity
options.B: Cranial cavity
options.C: Pelvic cavity
options.D: Spinal cavity

explanation: Great thinking! The spinal cavity is enclosed by the backbone (vertebral column) and holds the delicate spinal cord.

question: Why does the World Health Organization (WHO) classify FGM into different types?

options.A: To determine how much financial compensation the family receives
options.B: To predict exactly how many children a woman can safely deliver
options.C: To measure the exact extent of tissue removal and anatomical alteration
options.D: To decide which surgical instruments should be sterilized

explanation: Having a clear classification system helps us document injuries accurately so we can give each patient the right, tailored care.

question: What is the main purpose of tracking indicators in a PAC monitoring and evaluation system?

options.A: To publicly expose staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To calculate individual nurses' salaries based on procedure counts
options.C: To reduce the total number of patients visiting the health facility
options.D: To measure service performance, track outcomes, and guide quality improvement

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation helps managers see what is working well and where gaps exist, so the facility can continuously improve patient care.

question: What is the term for an infection that jumps naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infection
options.B: Autoimmune condition
options.C: Zoonotic disease
options.D: Hereditary disorder

explanation: Zoonotic diseases (or zoonoses) are the ones we share with animals. Animals are usually the main reservoir here!

question: How do targeted therapy drugs differ from traditional chemotherapy?

options.A: They work exclusively by boosting the overall white blood cell count in the bloodstream
options.B: They can only be taken as topical creams applied directly to skin lesions
options.C: They completely rebuild the patient's bone marrow within forty-eight hours of administration
options.D: They focus on specific molecular targets involved in tumor growth rather than attacking all dividing cells

explanation: You're doing great! Targeted therapies act like smart missiles, zeroing in on specific cancer proteins instead of harming all fast-growing cells.

question: How does health education during antenatal clinics directly help an expectant mother?

options.A: It removes the need for physical examinations by the doctor
options.B: It guarantees that her baby will sleep through the night
options.C: It builds her confidence and encourages positive health behaviors
options.D: It completely stops her from ever experiencing physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Knowledge gives mums confidence, calms their fears, and guides them to take great care of themselves and their growing baby.

question: Which type of food is best for adding bulk to stool and keeping constipation away?

options.A: Refined sugars and simple carbohydrates
options.B: High-fiber foods like vegetables and whole grains
options.C: Red meats and processed sausages
options.D: Highly processed dairy products

explanation: Fiber is a superstar! It adds bulk and softness to stool, helping things move smoothly through the bowels.

question: A student nurse uses old patient admission files from last year to study malaria rates. What kind of data source is this?

options.A: Subjective data source
options.B: Secondary data source
options.C: Primary data source
options.D: Experimental data source

explanation: Because someone else collected those files in the past, you are using a secondary source. It's like hand-me-down data!

question: Why might a patient in early shock still have a normal blood pressure reading?

options.A: Blood pressure monitors are usually inaccurate in emergencies
options.B: Kidneys immediately stop producing urine to save pressure
options.C: Fluid volume only affects the health of the heart
options.D: The body uses compensatory mechanisms like vasoconstriction

explanation: Our amazing bodies fight back! The nervous system tightens blood vessels and speeds up the heart to keep blood pressure normal at first, even if fluid is low.

question: Why is priority setting such an important step in community health nursing?

options.A: Health laws prohibit nurses from tackling more than one disease
options.B: Most communities only ever experience a single health issue
options.C: It ensures that minor problems are always treated before major ones
options.D: Resources are never enough to solve every health problem at once

explanation: Exactly! Because time, money, and staff are always limited, we have to prioritize which issues need our immediate attention.

question: When a patient uses a single-point cane for walking, which hand should hold the cane?

options.A: The hand on the stronger side
options.B: The hand on the weaker side
options.C: Both hands must hold the handle
options.D: Whichever hand is most dominant

explanation: Holding the cane on the strong side allows the patient to lean weight onto it while moving the opposite weak leg forward. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which mineral found in fruits helps to lower and regulate blood pressure?

options.A: Magnesium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Sodium

explanation: Spot on! Potassium is fantastic for the heart because it helps ease tension in your blood vessel walls, keeping your blood pressure steady.

question: What is a primary sign of compassion fatigue in a healthcare worker?

options.A: A sudden increase in physical body weight and strength
options.B: Excessive excitement and eagerness for every shift
options.C: Extraordinary patience with difficult administrative tasks
options.D: Emotional numbness and exhaustion from constant caregiving

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when exposure to continuous suffering drains a nurse's emotional reserves, causing burnout and detachment. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h7)

question: Why does a patient with severe burns need a high calorie diet?

options.A: Excessive fluid retention in the lower limbs
options.B: Poor absorption of dietary water
options.C: Rapid tissue breakdown and high metabolism
options.D: Low baseline systemic blood pressure

explanation: Severe burns put the body into a hypermetabolic state where it breaks down its own tissues rapidly. Extra calories help fuel that healing process!

question: What simple question did Bernardino Ramazzini say doctors must always ask their patients?

options.A: What is your occupation?
options.B: How many hours do you sleep?
options.C: Where do you buy your food?
options.D: What is your family medical history?

explanation: Ramazzini realized that a patient's job is often the biggest clue to what is making them sick. Always remember to check your patient's work background!

question: What is a common tool managers use to check how happy and satisfied staff are?

options.A: Monthly hospital pharmacy audits
options.B: Anonymous employee satisfaction surveys
options.C: Mandatory physician credentialing files
options.D: Daily patient vital sign flow sheets

explanation: Anonymous surveys let nurses speak their minds freely and honestly about what's working and what's frustrating on the ward.

question: Why can transitioning from a hospital to home care be tough for a nurse?

options.A: Hospitals use entirely different medical terminology.
options.B: Hospitals do not teach any clinical procedures.
options.C: Home care requires autonomous decision-making without immediate medical backup.
options.D: Nurses in hospitals never interact with patients directly.

explanation: Correct! In the hospital, doctors and senior colleagues are close by. In home care, you often have to think and act independently.

question: Who on the healthcare team mainly helps patients with swallowing problems?

options.A: Speech-Language Pathologist
options.B: Occupational Therapist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Physical Therapist

explanation: Spot on! Speech therapists don't just help with talking—they are experts at checking if swallowing is safe, too.

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why must a mother with mastitis keep removing milk from the infected breast?

options.A: Pumping removes the need to take prescribed antibiotics
options.B: Stopping milk removal cures the infection faster
options.C: Continued drainage prevents further milk stasis and reduces infection severity
options.D: It prevents the baby from getting any nutrition

explanation: Emptying the breast stops milk from sitting stagnant, which is what bacteria love. Keeping it flowing helps her heal faster!

question: What do we mean by 'gender norms'?

options.A: Genetic markers inherited from parents
options.B: Medical guidelines for reproductive health
options.C: Fixed biological limits of the human body
options.D: Societal rules dictating expected behaviors

explanation: Great job! Gender norms are simply the unwritten rules or cultural standards that society uses to guide how men and women 'should' act.

question: What do we call nutrients that our bodies cannot make on their own, so we must get them from our food?

options.A: Secondary metabolites
options.B: Synthetic polymers
options.C: Endogenous proteins
options.D: Essential nutrients

explanation: Spot on! Essential nutrients are the ones your body can't manufacture by itself, so eating them is a must for survival.

question: Which vitamin does the liver desperately need to build several key clotting factors?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin B12
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Vitamin K is like a vital tool in the liver's workshop. Without it, clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X cannot be built.

question: Why should a nurse take every report of cramping in pregnancy seriously?

options.A: Milder aches can sometimes mask or precede serious complications.
options.B: All pregnant women require immediate bed rest for any pain.
options.C: Pain medications are mandatory for any reported discomfort.
options.D: Cramping always indicates an active uterine infection.

explanation: Even though most cramps are completely normal, checking them out helps us make sure we don't miss important warning signs like an ectopic pregnancy or preterm labor. Great nursing instincts!

question: How many unique identifiers must you use to make sure you have the right patient?

options.A: Three completely different family members
options.B: Only one verbal confirmation
options.C: At least two unique identifiers
options.D: No identifiers if you already know them

explanation: Always check at least two things—like their name and hospital ID band—even if you know their face well. It's a quick habit that prevents big mix-ups!

question: What type of white blood cell primarily produces antibodies?

options.A: Plasma cells
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Killer T-cells
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Plasma cells develop from B-lymphocytes and are the specialized cells that mass-produce and secrete antibodies into body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is keeping strict confidentiality so important when young adults come for reproductive health services?

options.A: It speeds up the registration process in busy outpatient departments
options.B: It ensures the clinic receives extra funding from the government
options.C: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek care without fear of stigma
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to document patient interactions

explanation: Exactly! Young people especially worry about gossip. When they know their secrets are safe with you, they will gladly seek help without fear. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is a major trap to avoid when writing specific objectives for your nursing proposal?

options.A: Using action verbs at the beginning of every sentence
options.B: Ensuring the objectives are measurable and realistic
options.C: Aligning the objectives with the research methodology
options.D: Creating too many objectives that make the study lose focus

explanation: Having a laundry list of twenty specific objectives will scatter your energy and make data collection a nightmare. Keep your list tight and relevant! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h7)

question: What dangerous event happens when severe swelling inside the skull pushes brain tissue downward?

options.A: Brain herniation
options.B: Ventriculomegaly
options.C: Cortical atrophy
options.D: Neural regeneration

explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work!

question: What is the big advantage of using a moist cold compress instead of a stiff ice pack?

options.A: They require no refrigeration or ice whatsoever
options.B: They completely eliminate the risk of frostbite
options.C: They mold easily to uneven body contours like the jaw or face
options.D: They stay warm for up to twelve hours at a time

explanation: You got it! Faces and jaws aren't flat, so a flexible moist compress hugs those tricky curves much better than a rigid ice pack.

question: What is a major danger of a severe Vitamin A deficiency in young children?

options.A: Extreme weight gain and early childhood obesity
options.B: Permanent softening of the bones resembling rickets
options.C: Uncontrolled bleeding due to lack of blood clotting factors
options.D: Increased risk of severe infections like measles and blindness

explanation: Vitamin A is a hero for eye health and immunity. Without it, kids are much more vulnerable to serious infections like measles, plus vision problems.

question: When we talk about 'nutrient quality' in a meal, what are we really looking at?

options.A: The physical weight of the food on the plate
options.B: The total number of calories in a meal
options.C: How well the body absorbs and uses food compounds
options.D: How long the food item can be stored safely

explanation: You've got this! Nutrient quality is all about how effectively your body can actually use what you eat, rather than just counting empty calories.

question: What is the decussation of the pyramids?

options.A: The fusion of the brainstem with the spinal cord
options.B: The crossing over of motor fibers to the opposite side
options.C: The production of fluid inside the brain ventricles
options.D: The separation of sensory nerves from motor nerves

explanation: Decussation simply means crossing over, which is why movement on one side of the body is controlled by the opposite brain hemisphere. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: Which health promotion approach focuses primarily on giving people information so they can make informed personal choices?

options.A: The educational approach
options.B: The quarantine approach
options.C: The purely surgical approach
options.D: The punitive penalty approach

explanation: The educational approach centers on knowledge sharing and building life skills to help people make healthier choices for themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a sample design in nursing research?

options.A: To write a budget for a hospital research project
options.B: To plan how to select a portion of the population to study
options.C: To interview hospital managers about staffing levels
options.D: To collect blood samples from patients safely

explanation: Spot on! A sample design is simply your game plan for choosing who will take part in your study so your findings make sense.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community health needs assessment?

options.A: To collect money from residents to build a private pharmacy
options.B: To fulfill government paperwork requirements without visiting the field
options.C: To discover actual health problems and disparities before planning action
options.D: To judge community members for poor hygiene practices

explanation: Exactly right! You have to know what's really going on before you can fix it. An assessment uncovers the true health challenges so you can target your help properly.

question: Why is depression in older adults frequently missed or left untreated?

options.A: Antidepressant medications work instantly in seniors
options.B: Symptoms are frequently mistaken for normal aging
options.C: Depression cures itself without any intervention
options.D: Older adults never experience depressive symptoms

explanation: It's sad but true—many people wrongly think that being withdrawn or feeling down is just 'part of growing old,' which causes them to miss treatable depression.

question: What is the route of transmission?

options.A: The time it takes for a disease to show its first symptoms
options.B: The specific path a pathogen takes from its source to a new host
options.C: The total number of microbes required to cause an infection
options.D: The chemical makeup of an infectious agent's outer shell

explanation: The route of transmission is simply the way a germ travels from where it lives to a person who can catch it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h1)

question: A nurse organizes a community screening program to check blood sugar levels in adults over forty. Which level of prevention does this represent?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed to find hidden health problems early so treatment can start right away, which is secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: What essential instruction must be given about sexual partners when treating infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Partners can continue unprotected intercourse during the treatment week.
options.B: Partners only need treatment if they develop severe abdominal pain.
options.C: Only partners with visible symptoms need prescription medication.
options.D: Sexual partners must be checked and treated at the same time.

explanation: Treating partners together is the only way to stop the annoying ping-pong game of passing the infection back and forth!

question: What is the main purpose of secondary health prevention in clinical practice?

options.A: Detecting diseases early before symptoms appear
options.B: Preventing an illness from ever starting
options.C: Treating advanced stages of chronic disease
options.D: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke

explanation: You got it! Secondary prevention is all about catching conditions early while treatment is still super effective.

question: What is a key action of the community health nurse acting as an advocate for unemployed persons?

options.A: Ensuring fair access to healthcare services without discrimination
options.B: Passing new national labor employment laws
options.C: Managing corporate factory hiring processes
options.D: Providing direct commercial loans for private business

explanation: Correct! Nursing advocacy is about protecting patient rights and ensuring financial hardship never blocks someone from getting medical care. Keep going! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h6)

question: Why do dementia units usually have secure, controlled exits?

options.A: To comply with federal fire safety codes for chemical storage rooms
options.B: To punish residents who refuse to participate in daily group activities
options.C: To restrict family members from visiting outside of strict morning hours
options.D: To prevent wandering and keep residents with memory loss safe

explanation: Correct! Wandering is very common in advanced dementia, so secure doors keep our vulnerable residents safe from getting lost.

question: What do we call a sudden, severe change in mental state where a patient becomes very confused and restless?

options.A: Chronic anemia
options.B: Stable hypertension
options.C: Mild osteoarthritis
options.D: Acute delirium

explanation: Delirium is a sudden, temporary state of confusion often seen in hospitalised patients. It puts them at risk of pulling out their IV lines or climbing out of bed unassisted.

question: A patient's eyes and optic nerves are uninjured, yet they cannot make sense of what they look at. Which lobe should the nurse suspect is affected?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Frontal lobe
options.C: Parietal lobe
options.D: Temporal lobe

explanation: The eyes gather light, but the occipital lobe processes and interprets the actual images we see. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h5)

question: When should a mother have her very first postnatal checkup after giving birth in a facility?

options.A: Only when the baby falls sick
options.B: When the child is ready for school
options.C: Within 24 hours of birth
options.D: At the end of the sixth week

explanation: Correct! The first 24 hours carry the highest risk for bleeding and newborn issues, so early checks are vital.

question: In research, what does 'generalizability' mean?

options.A: Using general medical terms instead of nursing jargon
options.B: Applying sample findings to a larger population
options.C: Keeping the research questions broad and vague
options.D: Ensuring all participants share the exact same age

explanation: You got it! Generalizability is about taking what we learned from a small group of patients and safely applying it to the wider patient community.

question: What is the main job of a bacteriostatic drug?

options.A: Neutralizing bacterial toxins in the blood
options.B: Stopping bacteria from multiplying
options.C: Instantly killing all bacterial cells
options.D: Destroying human white blood cells

explanation: Bacteriostatic drugs press 'pause' on bacterial growth and let the patient's immune system clean up the rest.

question: Which type of medicine is commonly given to prevent blood clots in patients with peripheral arterial disease?

options.A: Water pills (diuretics) that save potassium
options.B: Heart-stimulating drugs
options.C: Inhaled medicines for the lungs
options.D: Antiplatelet drugs like aspirin

explanation: Antiplatelet medications keep tiny blood cells (platelets) from sticking together on rough fatty plaques, helping to stop clots before they form.

question: What does a lot of leftover food ('plate waste') usually tell you about a meal?

options.A: That the kitchen budget is currently running a surplus
options.B: That the patients are eating far too much food
options.C: That the menu has too many different color varieties
options.D: A problem with food taste, texture, or acceptance

explanation: If food keeps coming back untouched, it usually means the patients aren't enjoying how it tastes or looks.

question: If a patient has severe liver disease and cannot make enough plasma proteins, what sign are they most likely to show?

options.A: Excessive dark stools
options.B: Generalized tissue swelling
options.C: Rapid hair loss
options.D: Sudden high fever

explanation: Spot on! Without enough albumin to hold fluid in the vessels, water leaks out into the body tissues, causing swelling (edema) that you will often see in clinical practice.

question: Which of these common patient habits is a major driver of antimicrobial resistance?

options.A: Taking prescribed antiviral medications for severe fungal skin rashes
options.B: Storing leftover medications in a cool, dark hospital refrigerator
options.C: Stopping prescribed antibiotic courses early before all bacteria are killed
options.D: Washing hands too frequently with standard antibacterial liquid soap

explanation: When patients stop antibiotics early, the toughest bacteria survive, multiply, and learn how to beat the drug next time!

question: What factor has the biggest influence on the overall survival outlook for a patient with a vulval tumour?

options.A: The stage of the cancer at the time of diagnosis
options.B: The specific brand of dressing used on the wound
options.C: The patient's personal preference for radiation therapy
options.D: The exact age of the patient during surgery

explanation: Well done! Catching the cancer early, before it spreads to the lymph nodes, gives the patient the best chance at long-term survival.

question: Which dangerous bacterial infection can easily enter through an open Guinea worm wound if someone isn't vaccinated?

options.A: Typhoid fever
options.B: Tetanus
options.C: Plague
options.D: Cholera

explanation: Well done! Open skin sores exposed to dirt are prime entry points for tetanus spores. This is why wound care and vaccination history matter so much in nursing!

question: What danger is associated with alarm fatigue in a busy ICU?

options.A: Nurses might miss critical changes in a patient's condition due to constant noise
options.B: Equipment batteries drain faster when alarms sound repeatedly
options.C: Patients sleep better because they get used to the background sounds
options.D: Doctors refuse to enter the unit until all monitors are silenced

explanation: When monitors beep constantly for non-emergencies, staff can become desensitized. You're doing great—staying alert to this helps keep patients safe!

question: Why are open-ended questions best when taking a drug history?

options.A: They are much faster to document in the nursing notes
options.B: They stop the patient from talking too much
options.C: They encourage the patient to share detailed, honest information
options.D: They prevent the patient from asking about their hospital bill

explanation: Open-ended questions let patients explain their routines in their own words instead of just saying yes or no. Excellent interviewing tip for the wards!

question: What do we call the outward, social way a person shows their grief?

options.A: Depression
options.B: Denial
options.C: Mourning
options.D: Suffering

explanation: Mourning is simply the visible, cultural, and social actions people take to express their grief after a loss.

question: Which condition is considered a high-risk factor that rules out a safe home delivery?

options.A: A normal vertex presentation at term
options.B: A history of a previous cesarean section
options.C: A history of a single normal spontaneous vaginal birth
options.D: A maternal age between twenty and thirty

explanation: Previous uterine scars carry a risk of uterine rupture during labor, making hospital delivery mandatory. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why is it so important to involve a speech-language pathologist early after a brain injury?

options.A: To prescribe appropriate mobility braces and walking frames
options.B: To coordinate home healthcare insurance and discharge funding
options.C: To manage chronic joint pain and muscle spasms in the limbs
options.D: To check for safe swallowing before the patient eats or drinks

explanation: Safety first! SLPs make sure patients can swallow food and water without choking, while also helping them find ways to communicate their needs.

question: During which gestational weeks is a routine GTT typically performed for pregnant women?
