options.A: Between 24 and 28 weeks
options.B: Between 8 and 12 weeks
options.C: Between 32 and 36 weeks
options.D: Immediately upon discovering the pregnancy

explanation: Gestational diabetes screening via GTT is standard practice during the late second trimester when placental hormones peak. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h2)

question: How should a nurse touch a newly applied plaster cast while it is still wet?

options.A: With the palms of the hands to avoid indentations
options.B: With a heating pad wrapped tightly around it
options.C: With rigid metal clamps for support
options.D: With the fingertips to check for soft spots

explanation: Always use your palms! Using your fingertips can leave deep dents in wet plaster, which press into the skin and cause painful sores.

question: Why might you suggest a patient eating plant-based iron (like beans or greens) drink a glass of orange juice with their meal?

options.A: Orange juice contains phytates that bind extra minerals
options.B: Citrus acid coats the stomach lining to prevent cramping
options.C: The sugar in the juice speeds up overall stomach emptying
options.D: Vitamin C in the juice enhances the absorption of plant-based iron

explanation: Brilliant! Vitamin C gives plant iron a chemical makeover that makes it way easier for your gut to absorb.

question: What makes controlling Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) so tricky in communities?

options.A: STIs cannot be transmitted if the infected person takes vitamins
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely unavailable in most health clinics
options.C: Many infections present with mild or silent symptoms
options.D: Antibiotics can cure viral infections just as easily as bacterial ones

explanation: Many STIs show zero signs at first! People feel totally fine, so they unknowingly spread the infection before realizing they need treatment.

question: What happens to the amount of oxygen a mother consumes during active labour contractions?

options.A: It increases significantly
options.B: It remains completely unchanged
options.C: It drops to zero
options.D: It fluctuates only at night

explanation: Labour is hard physical work! The body and contracting uterus need a lot more oxygen during this time. You're mastering midwifery concepts!

question: Why is knowing a drug's class super helpful when you meet an unfamiliar medication on the ward?

options.A: It tells the nurse the exact room temperature for storing the drug
options.B: It guarantees the patient will not experience any adverse reactions
options.C: It gives immediate clues about expected effects and side effects
options.D: It eliminates the need to check the hospital dosage calculations

explanation: Drugs in the same family share similar actions and side effects. Once you know the class, you already know a lot about how it behaves!

question: During the first assessment, why do nurses do medication reconciliation?

options.A: To avoid dangerous drug interactions
options.B: To prescribe new vitamins
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital drugs
options.D: To test the patient's memory

explanation: Checking all the drugs and supplements a patient is already taking helps you make sure new medications won't mix badly with them.

question: Why is sudden, heavy postpartum bleeding that causes dizziness treated as a top emergency?

options.A: It prevents the mother from producing enough breast milk
options.B: It quickly leads to hypovolemic shock and organ failure
options.C: It always results in permanent damage to the kidneys
options.D: It causes the baby to reject breastfeeding due to stress

explanation: Rapid blood loss starves vital organs of oxygen. Without fast intervention, the mother's body can slip into shock very quickly.

question: Why can relying solely on normal vital signs be misleading in a critically ill patient?

options.A: The body's compensatory mechanisms can hide internal decline for a while.
options.B: Normal ranges apply only to children, not adults.
options.C: Vital signs change every single second without reason.
options.D: Monitors are frequently broken in hospital environments.

explanation: Patients can push their heart rate and blood vessels to work harder to maintain normal numbers right up until their system suddenly crashes. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse scores low in medication safety during a review. What should the manager do next?

options.A: Establish a clear plan with check-ins to monitor medication practice improvement
options.B: Ignore the score since annual reviews do not impact daily clinical work
options.C: Reassign the nurse permanently to administrative duties without notice
options.D: Report the nurse directly to the national licensing board immediately

explanation: Good leaders don't just point out mistakes and walk away. They set up a supportive plan with regular check-ins to help you build your confidence and safety.

question: Why do some caregivers stop bringing their children for immunizations after the first few visits?

options.A: Infants develop permanent immunity from the very first injection
options.B: They do not realize that multiple doses are needed for full protection
options.C: Clinics automatically confiscate vaccination cards after six weeks
options.D: Government laws forbid children from receiving more than two visits

explanation: Spot on! Not knowing the full immunization schedule is a major reason parents fail to return for booster and final doses.

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of research in nursing?

options.A: Improving patient outcomes through proven interventions
options.B: Helping reduce ineffective and wasteful clinical procedures
options.C: Eliminating the need for nurses to ever think critically
options.D: Building a unique scientific foundation for the profession

explanation: That's right! Research actually requires MORE critical thinking, as we must thoughtfully apply evidence rather than replacing our brains.

question: Why do surgeons pump carbon dioxide gas into the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.A: To stimulate the patient's breathing rate
options.B: To create a working space and visualize organs clearly
options.C: To sterilize the surgical instruments automatically
options.D: To cool down the internal organs during the operation

explanation: Correct! The gas puffs up the tummy like a balloon, lifting the wall away from the organs so the surgeon has plenty of room to see and work safely.

question: How do you properly test Cranial Nerve VII (the Facial nerve)?

options.A: By asking the patient to identify different sweet and salty tastes
options.B: By observing facial symmetry while the patient smiles and frowns
options.C: By checking if the tongue stays straight when sticking it out
options.D: By testing the corneal blink reflex using a cotton wisp

explanation: Since CN VII controls facial expressions, watching if both sides of the face move evenly when they smile or frown is the best test!

question: In the 'Four Ps' of labour, what does 'passage' mean?

options.A: The maternal bony pelvis and soft birth canal
options.B: The size and presenting part of the fetus
options.C: The emotional state and anxiety level of the mother
options.D: The strength and frequency of uterine contractions

explanation: Think of the 'passage' as the road the baby travels through—the mother's pelvis and soft birth tissues.

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of the DRF pricing strategy?

options.A: Maintaining long-term fund sustainability
options.B: Maximizing commercial profit margins
options.C: Ensuring continuous availability of drugs
options.D: Keeping essential medicines affordable

explanation: Spot on! Public health DRFs aren't businesses trying to get rich; they are here to keep essential medicines within reach for everyday patients while keeping the fund alive.

question: Why is it so important to plan care goals together with the client and their family?

options.A: To shift all legal responsibility for treatment onto the family
options.B: Because care happens in their personal space and must fit their daily reality
options.C: Because hospital rules legally apply to all home settings
options.D: To make sure the nurse does not have to do any heavy lifting

explanation: You got it! As nurses visiting someone's home, our plan has to make sense for their everyday life, or it simply won't work.

question: What is the real difference between just hearing someone talk and active listening?

options.A: Active listening can only be performed in a quiet hospital office.
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to offer immediate medical diagnoses.
options.C: Active listening involves full concentration on both words and underlying emotions.
options.D: Hearing requires the nurse to write down every spoken word verbatim.

explanation: Active listening means tuning into the feelings behind the words, not just waiting for your turn to speak. Great nurses master this!

question: Why should you connect a health topic to the daily life experiences of adult learners?

options.A: Ministry regulations state that lectures must last for at least two hours
options.B: It prevents students from asking difficult questions about medications
options.C: Older individuals cannot memorize new information without a story
options.D: Adults learn best when the topic directly relates to their current life challenges

explanation: Exactly! When learners see how a topic solves their everyday problems, their motivation and memory skyrocket.

question: An elderly client living alone cannot walk well enough to go to the local market. What community resource can you suggest?

options.A: A commercial fast-food chain
options.B: A high-intensity exercise gym
options.C: A home-delivered meal program
options.D: An inpatient hospital admission

explanation: Brilliant! Meal-delivery services are a fantastic way to make sure clients with mobility issues still get proper nutrition at home.

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital during family planning sessions?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek needed care safely
options.B: It guarantees that the government will fund the clinic supplies
options.C: It prevents hospital administrators from auditing patient records
options.D: It stops family members from asking about the client's health

explanation: Clients need assurance that their private reproductive health details will not be shared openly in the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: A patient admitted to the ward mentions taking a local herbal concoction alongside prescribed blood pressure pills. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Order the patient to discard the herbal concoction immediately into the hospital bin
options.B: Double the dose of the blood pressure medication to counteract the herbal mixture
options.C: Tell the patient that traditional herbs never interact with modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Document the herbal concoction in the medication reconciliation record and inform the doctor

explanation: All substances must be recorded and evaluated for potential interactions before deciding the next clinical steps. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h4)

question: What should happen immediately after a patient's blood pressure check flags a high reading at a community health fair?

options.A: Immediate prescription of lifelong high blood pressure medication
options.B: Reassurance that screening tests are always fully accurate
options.C: Referral for formal diagnostic evaluation by a primary provider
options.D: Immediate admission to an intensive care hospital unit

explanation: Remember, a screening just raises a warning flag—it doesn't give a final diagnosis. The patient needs proper medical follow-up to confirm!

question: As a student nurse or midwife, what is a key way you can promote safe motherhood in your community?

options.A: Educating families on danger signs and encouraging hospital delivery
options.B: Paying the hospital transport bills for poor pregnant women personally
options.C: Performing major surgeries inside primary health centers without doctors
options.D: Making laws to punish traditional birth attendants who work in villages

explanation: Community health education saves lives! Teaching families what warning signs to look out for helps them get moms to the hospital before it's too late.

question: What critical warning signs should a nurse teach a post-abortion client before she leaves the clinic?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness in the morning
options.B: Severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, or high fever
options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

explanation: These symptoms are red flags that can indicate infection, retained tissue, or other complications requiring immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to practice self-awareness?

options.A: It helps the nurse hide personal feelings from the patient
options.B: It prevents the patient from asking too many personal questions
options.C: It allows the nurse to understand how personal biases affect care
options.D: It ensures the nurse finishes charting tasks much faster

explanation: Knowing your own background and biases helps you keep your interactions fair, professional, and focused purely on what the patient needs.

question: Why must nurses in local community clinics look beyond hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Environmental and economic living conditions heavily impact health outcomes
options.B: Nurses are forbidden from providing care outside of enclosed rooms
options.C: Community members never visit hospitals for severe medical problems
options.D: Lab tests can only be accurately performed in outdoor market stalls

explanation: Understanding a patient's home and community environment helps explain why illnesses occur and how to prevent them. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h6)

question: When are your kidneys most likely to start producing extra glucose?

options.A: Prolonged fasting or starvation
options.B: Excessive intake of dietary water
options.C: A sudden spike in blood pressure
options.D: Eating a large carbohydrate-rich meal

explanation: Exactly right! When liver energy stores run out during a long fast, the kidneys step up and make glucose to help keep your body fueled.

question: If a hospital team wants to figure out the clinical factors behind a recent rise in maternal deaths at their facility, what process should they join?

options.A: Public media campaigns advertising home delivery options
options.B: Random household door-to-door sisterhood surveys
options.C: Civil service tax exemption hearings for pregnant women
options.D: Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR) audits

explanation: MDSR audits bring healthcare workers together to review cases openly, spot what could have been avoided, and make patient care safer for the next mother.

question: Which workplace strategy shows that a hospital truly cares about long-term staff motivation?

options.A: Sponsoring specialty certifications and clear career ladders
options.B: Lowering entry-level salaries to save money for equipment
options.C: Reducing annual vacation days to increase bedside coverage
options.D: Eliminating all staff meetings to maximize shift hours

explanation: When a hospital helps you grow your skills and gives you clear paths to climb higher, you feel valued and ready to stay!

question: Why is the order of removing your PPE so important?

options.A: It prevents self-contamination from dirty gear onto clean skin
options.B: It keeps the patient's room looking tidy
options.C: It ensures the equipment can be washed and reused safely
options.D: It saves time during busy hospital shifts

explanation: Following the right steps ensures that the germs on your outer gear don't accidentally end up on your face or skin.

question: Why is looking at a trend of vital signs over several hours so much better than just checking a single set of numbers?

options.A: It is required for billing and insurance records
options.B: It proves the machine is working properly
options.C: It shows the direction the patient's health is moving
options.D: It replaces the need for physician physical exams

explanation: Exactly! Tracking numbers over time helps you spot a slow, steady slip in a patient's condition, even if their current numbers still technically look 'normal.'

question: During a physical exam for a patient with testicular torsion, which reflex is usually missing?

options.A: Cremasteric reflex
options.B: Patellar reflex
options.C: Gag reflex
options.D: Babinski reflex

explanation: Correct! Normally, stroking the inner thigh makes the testicle rise (cremasteric reflex). In torsion, that reflex is completely absent.

question: Why is sterilization stricter and more powerful than standard disinfection?

options.A: It only applies to items that touch intact human skin
options.B: It can be completed in a few seconds using simple wipes
options.C: It targets and kills bacterial spores as well as vegetative cells
options.D: It is performed using mild soaps and warm running water

explanation: Disinfection kills a lot of germs, but tough bacterial spores can survive it. Sterilization goes the extra mile to destroy those resilient spores completely!

question: Why do high-risk strains of HPV require regular cervical screening even when a woman feels fine?

options.A: High-risk HPV can cause silent cellular changes in the cervix that lead to cancer over time
options.B: Routine screening is the only way to clear the virus completely from nerve tissues
options.C: HPV bacteria become resistant to standard antibiotic therapies if left unchecked
options.D: The virus rapidly destroys red blood cells and causes severe systemic anemia

explanation: High-risk HPV can change cervical cells without causing any pain or warning signs. That's why routine Pap smears are so lifesaving!

question: A patient receives several bags of packed red blood cells after an accident, but no plasma. What clotting complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Vitamin K toxicity
options.B: Dilutive coagulopathy
options.C: Hereditary hemophilia A
options.D: Polycythemia vera

explanation: If you only pump in red blood cells without replacing plasma, you end up diluting the patient's remaining platelets and clotting factors. This is called dilutive coagulopathy.

question: What was the main focus of 'Selective Primary Health Care' introduced after the initial Alma-Ata momentum slowed?

options.A: Targeting specific, high-impact interventions for particular diseases
options.B: Stopping all vaccination programs to focus entirely on surgery
options.C: Handing over all health clinics to private international corporations
options.D: Building large multi-specialty teaching hospitals in every district

explanation: Selective PHC concentrated resources on specific, measurable disease interventions rather than broad, comprehensive health system building. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why do nurse researchers collect data in a study?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside shift reports completely
options.B: To prove that a chosen nursing theory is entirely wrong
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for the hospital
options.D: To gather information needed to answer a research question

explanation: Think of data collection like gathering clues to solve a case. You collect specific info to answer your main research question!

question: How can food fermentation actually improve nutrition?

options.A: It turns proteins into pure chemical preservatives
options.B: It completely destroys all mineral content in the food
options.C: It removes all carbohydrates so the food has zero calories
options.D: It increases the availability of certain nutrients and vitamins

explanation: Fermentation uses friendly microbes that help create extra vitamins and break down things in food that normally block mineral absorption. Pretty cool, right?

question: How does a female condom stay securely in place inside the vagina?

options.A: A flexible inner ring at the closed end
options.B: Suction created by an external pump
options.C: Sutures placed by a healthcare provider
options.D: An adhesive strip on the outside

explanation: You nailed it! The inner ring at the closed end helps the user push and anchor the pouch securely inside.

question: How do male champions help improve men's participation in family health?

options.A: By setting a positive example and discussing health openly among peers
options.B: By paying all the medical bills for families in the community
options.C: By taking over the duties of healthcare providers at the clinic
options.D: By forcing other men to visit hospitals through legal action

explanation: Respected peers break down cultural barriers by openly sharing their own positive experiences with clinic attendance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h6)

question: A patient having a severe allergic reaction has wheezing, swollen lips, and crashing blood pressure. What medication is given first?

options.A: Intramuscular epinephrine
options.B: Oral diphenhydramine
options.C: Subcutaneous insulin
options.D: Intravenous paracetamol

explanation: Brilliant! Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis because it quickly opens up the airways and brings blood pressure back up.

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when a patient arrives with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Stabilizing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Filling out legal police reports immediately
options.C: Conducting a detailed religious counseling session
options.D: Interrogating the patient about who performed the procedure

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Saving the patient's life and treating shock always takes priority over asking questions.

question: Why might a doctor order a biopsy for a vulval lump in an older adult patient?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of fluid inside the cyst
options.B: To check and make sure the persistent or unusual mass is not cancerous
options.C: To prove that the cyst started from an infected hair follicle
options.D: To help the fluid sac absorb faster on its own

explanation: Any unusual or stubborn lump in older women needs a quick tissue check (biopsy) just to be 100% sure it isn't malignant.

question: How does evaluation differ from monitoring in a community health program?

options.A: Evaluation is optional, whereas monitoring is required by international law
options.B: Evaluation focuses entirely on staff discipline, while monitoring deals with drug supplies
options.C: Evaluation assesses the final outcomes and impact, while monitoring tracks ongoing daily activities
options.D: Evaluation is done before any data is collected, while monitoring happens only at the end

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring checks the process as it happens day-to-day, while evaluation measures the final results and overall success of the project.

question: What is the main purpose of a community diagnosis?

options.A: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy volunteers
options.B: To manage the financial budget of a primary health clinic
options.C: To treat individual patients in a hospital ward
options.D: To assess the overall health status and needs of a population

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at an entire group of people to find out their health problems, resources, and needs rather than focusing on just one patient. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: When a client wants to switch to a different birth control method during a follow-up visit, what is your main job as a nurse?

options.A: Charge an extra administrative fee for changing the care plan
options.B: Refuse service until a senior medical officer approves the change
options.C: Force the client to continue the original method for at least one more year
options.D: Ensure there is no gap in contraceptive coverage to prevent unintended pregnancy

explanation: When changing methods, timing is everything. We must make sure there is no unprotected gap where an unintended pregnancy could happen.

question: How do nursing theorists define 'health' within our professional framework?

options.A: A dynamic state of physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The complete elimination of all hospital admissions nationwide
options.C: The total absence of any identifiable bacteria in the blood
options.D: A static condition achieved strictly through pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health isn't just the literal absence of sickness. In nursing, we see it as a flowing, everyday state of overall physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which sign tells you a mixed lotion should be thrown away immediately?

options.A: A label showing it was mixed three days ago
options.B: Visible separation or discoloration
options.C: A smooth and uniform texture throughout
options.D: A slight cooling sensation upon skin contact

explanation: If the cream separates or changes color, it means it has gone bad and is no longer safe to use. You're doing great!

question: Why are patients with long-term diabetes at high risk for foot ulcers and amputations?

options.A: Nerve damage and poor blood flow reduce feeling and healing
options.B: Daily physical exercise wears down the bones in the lower legs
options.C: High blood sugar makes the skin on the feet extremely fragile
options.D: Patients naturally lose interest in cleaning and drying their feet

explanation: Neuropathy prevents patients from feeling minor injuries, while poor circulation stops those injuries from healing properly, leading to severe ulcers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h6)

question: What is a major practical challenge when trying to prosecute FGM offenders in local Nigerian courts?

options.A: Mandatory legalization of the practice by state governors
options.B: Complete absence of any federal or state legal frameworks
options.C: Immunity granted to all traditional practitioners by the constitution
options.D: Lack of training and logistical support for police and judiciary

explanation: Correct! Law enforcement officers sometimes struggle to investigate and take these cases to court due to limited resources and specialized training.

question: What decides how thick or watery a colostomy stool will be?

options.A: The anatomical location of the stoma along the large intestine
options.B: The amount of physical exercise the patient does every day
options.C: The time of day the patient eats their main meal
options.D: The exact brand of the appliance pouch the patient wears

explanation: Exactly! Stool gets thicker the longer it travels through the colon because more water is absorbed along the way.

question: What do we call citizens who are forced to leave their homes because of conflicts or floods?

options.A: Orphans and Vulnerable Children
options.B: Internally Displaced Persons
options.C: Persons with Disabilities
options.D: Corporate health executives

explanation: When people are forced to flee within their own country (IDPs), they often live in temporary camps and rely heavily on special community health outreaches.

question: When taking off dirty gloves, where should your very first move begin?

options.A: Tearing the palm area to loosen a tight fit
options.B: Pulling straight from the fingertips
options.C: Grasping the outside of the cuff and peeling downward
options.D: Snapping the wristband outward with a quick flick

explanation: Pinching the outer cuff lets you peel the glove inside out, trapping all the nasty germs safely on the inside.

question: Why do adolescent peer groups often create challenges in reproductive health education?

options.A: Peers frequently spread misinformation about contraception and infection risks.
options.B: Peers are legally permitted to prescribe medications to each other.
options.C: Peers always hold the exact same cultural values as parents.
options.D: Peers refuse to talk about personal relationships entirely.

explanation: Adolescents often rely on friends for advice on sensitive topics, which can lead to acting on dangerous myths rather than medical facts. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h4)

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in nursing and public health?

options.A: Information, Education, and Communication
options.B: Infection, Evaluation, and Control
options.C: Investigation, Education, and Counselling
options.D: Immunization, Environment, and Care

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are the core pillars of public health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is a crucial check a nurse must do before giving any mucous membrane medication?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for two minutes
options.B: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly over the site
options.C: Crush the medication to speed up local absorption
options.D: Inspect the target membrane for irritation or lesions

explanation: Always take a quick look first! Checking the tissue ensures there are no open sores or heavy irritation that could make absorption painful or unsafe for the patient.

question: A client with asthma is wheezing heavily during an acute attack. What is the primary physical reason for this sound?

options.A: Fluid pooling at the very base of the lungs
options.B: Rough pleural linings rubbing together with each breath
options.C: Air passing through narrowed, constricted airways
options.D: Thick mucus vibrating inside the upper trachea

explanation: Wheezes are high-pitched musical sounds produced when air is forced through airways narrowed by bronchospasm, swelling, or mucus. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h4)

question: How can a nurse help ensure a patient on a soft diet gets enough nutrition?

options.A: Encouraging nutrient-dense additions like cream soups and smoothies
options.B: Insisting the patient eat dry crackers for extra fiber
options.C: Limiting fluid intake during meal times
options.D: Replacing all meals with plain water

explanation: Adding calorie- and nutrient-dense items helps make up for smaller meal portions without requiring extra chewing. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h6)

question: Which complication involves dangerous pressure build-up inside an enclosed muscle compartment that cuts off blood supply?

options.A: Avascular necrosis
options.B: Fat embolism syndrome
options.C: Compartment syndrome
options.D: Osteomyelitis infection

explanation: Compartment syndrome occurs when swelling restricted by tight fascia compresses blood vessels and nerves, threatening limb survival. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h9)

question: What is the main reason labs use differential growth media?

options.A: To completely kill off all unwanted bacteria in a clinical sample
options.B: To preserve the live bacterial sample in the refrigerator for many months
options.C: To increase the total physical size of individual bacterial cells for easy viewing
options.D: To tell different bacteria apart by showing color changes from their chemical reactions

explanation: Well done! Differential media use color changes right on the Petri dish so lab techs can easily spot which bacteria is which.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when starting a Behavioural Change Communication project?

options.A: Evaluating final program financial costs
options.B: Punishing non-compliant community members
options.C: Assessment and formative research
options.D: Mass media television broadcasting

explanation: Correct! Before designing any messages, you have to talk to the community to find out what they already know and what they actually need.

question: A home care nurse gets stuck in terrible traffic and flooded roads on the way to a patient. What is the immediate effect of this delay?

options.A: The patient's medication chart gets permanently misplaced.
options.B: The nursing agency automatically loses its operating license.
options.C: The patient's medical insurance policy becomes invalid.
options.D: Scheduled administration of vital treatments or assessments is delayed.

explanation: Correct! Bad traffic means care and medications arrive late. It's a common challenge for community nurses!

question: Why is epidemiologic data vital for community health nurses?

options.A: It eliminates the need for physical examinations in clinics
options.B: It replaces the need to interview sick community members
options.C: It guarantees that funding will increase every fiscal year
options.D: It helps plan effective prevention and allocate resources wisely

explanation: Having accurate data allows nurses to target interventions where they are needed most to protect the community. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h1)

question: A patient stands up, closes their eyes, and immediately starts swaying heavily and losing balance. How do we document this?

options.A: Positive Romberg test
options.B: Positive Brudzinski sign
options.C: Presence of resting tremor
options.D: Normal cerebellar function

explanation: That's a positive Romberg test! It happens when a patient can stand fine with their eyes open (using vision to balance), but loses it when they close their eyes.

question: What is the main role of peer educators in youth-friendly health programs?

options.A: Performing minor surgical procedures in community schools
options.B: Bridging the gap by sharing health info and encouraging clinic visits
options.C: Enforcing hospital rules on visiting adult patients
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of the local hospital

explanation: Teens trust their peers! Peer educators are fantastic at spreading positive health habits and helping friends feel safe visiting the clinic.

question: Why should nurses avoid using heavy medical jargon when speaking with community patients?

options.A: Medical terms are forbidden in primary health care clinics
options.B: Using simple words takes too much time during consultations
options.C: It shows that the nurse lacks proper professional training
options.D: Patients may misunderstand their diagnosis and fail to follow treatment

explanation: Using everyday language ensures the patient truly grasps what is wrong and what they need to do to get better. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h3)

question: Where does a primary health clinic in Nigeria send its monthly injection safety report first?

options.A: The Local Government Area (LGA) focal officer
options.B: The international donor agency headquarters
options.C: The nearest private pharmaceutical distributor
options.D: Directly to the Federal Minister of Health

explanation: Correct! Reports start locally at the LGA level before moving upward to the state and federal tables.

question: What is a key nursing priority when caring for a patient with a new suprapubic catheter after bladder surgery?

options.A: Clamp the drainage tubing tightly every two hours to train the bladder muscles.
options.B: Change the catheter insertion tract daily using dry gauze pads only.
options.C: Ensure the tubing stays unobstructed and check the insertion site for leaking urine or infection.
options.D: Flush the drainage system forcefully with sterile water if urine output slows down.

explanation: Keeping the tube clear and watching the site keeps urine flowing smoothly and stops germs from causing an infection. You've got this nursing routine down!

question: What is a major sign of a 'Theory X' nurse manager?

options.A: Relying on strict rules, surveillance, and micromanagement
options.B: Believing that staff naturally find clinical work fulfilling
options.C: Encouraging nurses to take full autonomy over care plans
options.D: Involving junior nurses in hospital policymaking

explanation: Theory X managers assume staff dislike work and need to be watched constantly. They love strict rules and heavy supervision rather than trusting their nurses.

question: Which special cells in your stomach lining pump out hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: G cells
options.C: Mucous cells
options.D: Parietal cells

explanation: You've got it. Parietal cells are the stomach's acid factories, producing both the hydrochloric acid needed for digestion and intrinsic factor to help absorb vitamin B12.

question: What does informed consent require before a client receives a contraceptive method?

options.A: Proof of employment and stable monthly income
options.B: A written letter of approval from a community chief
options.C: Complete agreement from the client's extended family
options.D: Full understanding of benefits, risks, and correct usage

explanation: Informed consent means the client knows what to expect, including how the method works and its potential side effects, before they choose it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: Who counts as a 'food handler' in a hospital or school setting?

options.A: Only the head chef in charge of the menu
options.B: The health inspector who visits monthly
options.C: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or utensils during prep or serving
options.D: Patients who eat the food provided

explanation: Anyone who comes into contact with food, plates, or cooking tools is considered a food handler. Safety starts with everyone!

question: What is the main difference between static and dynamic balance?

options.A: Static equilibrium deals with head position at rest, while dynamic equilibrium responds to movement.
options.B: Static equilibrium uses the eyes only, while dynamic equilibrium uses the ears.
options.C: Static equilibrium controls heart rate, while dynamic equilibrium controls breathing.
options.D: Static equilibrium occurs only in water, while dynamic equilibrium occurs on land.

explanation: Think of it this way: static is staying still against gravity, while dynamic is when you are moving or turning around! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h1)

question: Where does the urinary bladder sit in relation to the uterus in females?

options.A: Lateral to the right and left ovaries
options.B: Directly posterior to the rectal wall
options.C: Posterior and superior to the uterus
options.D: Anterior and inferior to the uterus

question: How does severe poverty make it much harder for someone to escape an abusive relationship?

options.A: It stops community members from offering emotional comfort
options.B: It prevents healthcare facilities from providing physical examinations
options.C: It creates financial dependence that makes leaving the abuser extremely difficult
options.D: It automatically removes all legal rights from the victim in court

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in eclampsia?

options.A: Oxytocin infusion
options.B: Diazepam injection
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Sodium bicarbonate

question: Why is it important for a nurse to keep a wide stance and bend their knees when lifting or moving a patient?

question: A community health nurse notices an increase in diarrhea cases during the rainy season. What is the best immediate action?

options.B: Ordering advanced genetic testing for all community members
options.C: Recommending immediate surgical procedures for every household

question: What is the sneaky trick that bacterial enzymes like beta-lactamase pull off?

options.A: They help bacteria digest human red blood cells
options.B: They destroy specific antibiotic medications
options.C: They speed up bacterial cell division
options.D: They create a thick capsule around the cell

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?

options.A: Post-infectious immunity

options.C: Acute viral syndrome
options.D: Long COVID

question: What is the term for severe, widespread swelling that affects the entire body?

options.A: Anasarca
options.B: Ascites
options.C: Ischemia
options.D: Cyanosis

question: A new mother soaks two heavy pads in twenty minutes and feels dizzy. What should you suspect?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage

options.D: Gestational trophoblastic disease

question: Which part of the glucometer setup has the chemical reagents that react with blood?

options.A: The digital display

options.D: The battery compartment

question: Why is the powerful drug Amphotericin B kept strictly for severe, life-threatening fungal infections?

options.A: It is completely ineffective against superficial mucosal yeast infections

question: Which drug is a main part of the preferred first-line HIV treatment guidelines in Nigeria?

options.A: Dolutegravir

question: How do parks and tree-lined streets help clean up city air?

options.A: They increase the temperature of the city to destroy bacteria

options.C: They produce chemical gases that neutralize industrial smoke

question: A patient arrives at the clinic 30 minutes after multiple wasp stings complaining of throat tightness and dizziness. What is your very first assessment?

options.A: Airway patency and respiratory status
